verdict.root_cause: Payment went silent mid-window (~23:15) on a normal info-level transaction completion, with no shutdown, crash, or re-bind record afterwards and unchanged process identity and service version [tr_041fbef7b9d5]. About four minutes later every sampled checkout trace fails in PaymentService/Charge with gRPC Unavailable name-resolution, ~0.0ms duration and 0% of trace time, meaning the client never opened a connection [tr_f4248832d4ea]. That is the signature of a payment process that stopped doing work while not exiting cleanly: it drops out of discovery and callers fail fast on resolution. Checkout is the alerter, not the culprit — its other dependencies (cart/Redis, currency, catalog, shipping, flagd) are clean in the same traces [tr_f4248832d4ea], and its aggregate error ratio shows no new excursion [tr_c73ae4c5dcef].
verdict.reasoning: Traces localise the failure to exactly one hop — checkout's Charge call — and the zero-duration name-resolution error rules out a slow backend or client timeout [tr_f4248832d4ea]. Payment's own logs stop at a healthy transaction and show no crash, restart or version change, so the instance neither died loudly nor was replaced [tr_041fbef7b9d5]. Change records are exculpatory for the configuration hypotheses: payment's traffic-shaping sidecar was removed ~22h before onset leaving no delay in effect [tr_352f01e4dff7], and checkout's CURRENCY_ADDR flapping ended 16.5h before onset and touches currency, not payment, while currency spans are error-free [tr_08b3cdb0176e, tr_f4248832d4ea]. Checkout's metrics show no new service-wide error spike, consistent with checkout merely relaying a downstream failure [tr_c73ae4c5dcef].
open_questions: No payment-side evidence distinguishes a frozen process from a payment instance severed from the network: payment logs were truncated and the final minutes contain no lines at all, so we never saw whether payment itself complained about unreachable peers [tr_041fbef7b9d5].

Payment's span-metrics series is empty across both incident and baseline windows, so request rate and latency for payment were never measured and its liveness cannot be confirmed independently [tr_2cea50f0ea84].
Checkout emitted zero log lines across the entire window, so its client-side view of resolution failures is unverified outside traces [tr_77a8b350df33].
No dispatch examined service discovery / DNS itself, which is the alternative source of a name-resolution failure with zero addresses.

alternatives.root_cause: Payment is running but cut off from the network/service registry, so its endpoints are withdrawn and checkout's resolver returns no addresses.
alternatives.why_not: Indistinguishable from a freeze on the caller side, but a partitioned-yet-running payment would normally still log its own failures to reach dependencies; the retained log lines end on a clean success with nothing after [tr_041fbef7b9d5]. Weakly demoted — log truncation means absence here is not strong proof.

alternatives.root_cause: Service discovery or DNS for the payment name is broken, so checkout resolves zero addresses while payment itself is healthy.
alternatives.why_not: No change record touches payment's name, port or registration — every payment change is a sidecar attach/remove [tr_352f01e4dff7] — and payment's own logs stopping at the same time is better explained by payment than by a resolver fault that would leave payment chattering normally [tr_041fbef7b9d5].

proposal.expected_effect: Recreating payment's container should restore a live, discoverable payment process. Two observations should follow: (1) in Tempo, new checkout PlaceOrder traces stop carrying an errored PaymentService/Charge child with gRPC Unavailable / name-resolution and ~0.0ms duration, and instead show a Charge span with non-trivial duration and OK status; (2) in Loki, {service="payment"} resumes emitting lines — first process startup/bind records (absent before, per tr_041fbef7b9d5), then the info-severity, trace-correlated transaction-completion records from the payment-logger scope that stopped at ~23:15. Secondary, weaker: checkout/frontend/frontend-proxy spans stop propagating the card-charge failure to the load generator. Checkout's aggregate error ratio is not a useful confirmation signal here — tr_c73ae4c5dcef shows it bursty and unchanged, so do not judge on it.
proposal.if_wrong: If, 5 minutes after the recreate, sampled checkout traces still show PaymentService/Charge failing at ~0.0ms with Unavailable/name-resolution and zero addresses, the fault is not payment's process state — it is name resolution or service discovery itself (never dispatched in this investigation), or an environment-level network severance that container recreate did not undo. A second falsifier: payment emits fresh startup and transaction lines in Loki (so the process is demonstrably alive and logging) while callers still get zero addresses — that isolates the fault squarely in discovery/DNS, not in payment. Note the asymmetry: payment has no span-metrics series at all in either window (tr_2cea50f0ea84), so payment-side liveness cannot be confirmed from metrics; confirmation rests entirely on traces from checkout and on payment's own log stream resuming.
proposal.risk: Not none. If payment was in fact alive and the failure is in DNS/service discovery, this takes down a working process for the duration of the recreate, converting a resolution failure into a real outage window, and destroys the frozen process's state — thread dumps, socket table, in-process evidence — which is the only thing that could have distinguished a freeze from a network severance. Any in-flight charges at the moment of recreate are lost, and in-process cache is discarded (rebuild cost on first requests). The restart is also irreversible: if the freeze was caused by something that re-manifests, we will have erased the one clean specimen of it.
proposal.blast_radius: payment itself, for the length of the container recreate. Its direct caller checkout sees connection reset / continued Unavailable during that interval; the failure already propagates checkout -> frontend -> frontend-proxy -> load-generator per tr_f4248832d4ea, so those three see it too, and user-visible checkout remains failing until payment re-registers. The order-completion consumers in the blast radius — fraud-detection, accounting, email — see no new orders during the window and a resumption after. cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping and flagd are untouched and were already clean in the same traces.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service failure starting at checkout and spreading to fraud-detection, payment, accounting and email within minutes; no open incident covers it. Origin is unclear between a checkout deploy and a shared dependency, so the fault class stays unknown.
